findings.title: TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: In EventManager.create, mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar ?? []. If destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined, but the next line reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. This will throw a TypeError for Google Meet events that have no destination calendar, breaking booking creation.

findings.title: Video credentialId is no longer stored in references created by EventManager.create
findings.body: referencesToCreate now sets credentialId only when the result is a calendar result. Previously, non-calendar results preserved result.credentialId. As a result, video booking references can be created with credentialId undefined. Later cancellation or update flows that look up the video credential by reference.credentialId may fail to delete or update the meeting.

findings.title: updateEvent can be called with undefined or stale credential
findings.body: In updateAllCalendarEvents, when a booking reference has credentialId, the code assigns credential from in-memory credentials or the database. If no credential is found, credential may remain undefined or retain the value from a previous loop iteration, and updateEvent is still pushed. This can cause updates to fail or be attempted with the wrong credential.

findings.title: Only the first old calendar reference is deleted when merging bookings
findings.body: When newBookingId is provided, updateAllCalendarEvents deletes the old calendar event by finding only the first booking reference whose type includes _calendar. For collective or multi-host bookings there can be multiple calendar references, so the remaining old calendar events will not be deleted and can remain on host calendars.

findings.title: Fallback credential filter looks for exact type calendar
findings.body: createAllCalendarEvents falls back to this.calendarCredentials.filter(cred => cred.type === 'calendar') when no destinationCalendar is present. Calendar credential types are normally values like google_calendar or office365_calendar, so this exact equality will usually match nothing. The stated fallback to the first connected calendar will therefore not create any calendar event.

findings.title: Possible duplicate creation for other_calendar integrations
findings.body: createAllCalendarEvents first creates events for each entry in event.destinationCalendar, then unconditionally creates events for every credential whose type includes other_calendar. If a destinationCalendar entry is itself an other_calendar credential, the same integration event can be created twice.

findings.title: updateLocation can create booking references without credential or external calendar identifiers
findings.body: updateLocation maps results into referencesToCreate using result.externalId and result.credentialId. Calendar update results from CalendarManager.updateEvent do not populate these fields, so calendar references produced by updateLocation can have undefined credentialId and externalCalendarId. Handlers that persist these references may store incomplete reference rows.

findings.title: Team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: For collective team events, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null when neither eventType nor organizer has a destinationCalendar. The later call evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) then does nothing because of optional chaining on null. Hosts' destination calendars are silently lost, so their calendar events may not be created.

findings.title: Organization slug logic was inverted for billing-enabled and billing-disabled environments
findings.body: The previous code set slug when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED was false and set metadata.requestedSlug when it was true. The new code sets slug when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true and omits slug when billing is disabled. This changes organization creation behavior and can create organizations without a slug when billing is disabled or with a slug prematurely when billing is enabled.

findings.title: Google updateEvent lost its fallback to a destination calendar
findings.body: selectedCalendar is set to externalCalendarId when truthy; otherwise it searches event.destinationCalendar for a calendar whose externalId === externalCalendarId. When externalCalendarId is null or undefined, this lookup cannot find anything and selectedCalendar becomes undefined. Existing references without externalCalendarId will cause Google event updates to be called with an undefined calendarId instead of falling back to the event's destination calendar.

findings.title: Google deleteEvent fallback can target the wrong calendar
findings.body: deleteEvent now only uses externalCalendarId when provided; otherwise it attempts to find a destination calendar with externalId === externalCalendarId, which is undefined when no externalCalendarId was passed. It then falls back to primary. If the event exists on a non-primary calendar and externalCalendarId is missing, deletion can fail silently with a 404 or leave the event on the correct calendar.

findings.title: Google event patch can use undefined calendarId
findings.body: createEvent inserts the event with calendarId selectedCalendar || 'primary', but the subsequent events.patch call uses calendarId: selectedCalendar without the same fallback. If selectedCalendar is undefined, the patch request can fail even though the event was created on primary.

findings.title: Google createEvent ignores destination externalId when credentialId is absent
findings.body: createEvent now chooses the Google calendar by finding a destinationCalendar entry with the same credentialId. Older or incomplete destinationCalendar records may have externalId but no credentialId. In that case the service falls back to primary, whereas the previous behavior could use destinationCalendar.externalId. This can create events on the wrong calendar after the migration to arrays.

findings.title: Lark createEvent only uses the first destination calendar for multi-host events
findings.body: LarkCalendarService.createEvent destructures the first entry from event.destinationCalendar and ignores the credential that is creating the event. When EventManager creates events for multiple hosts, each host's credential receives the same full destinationCalendar array, but Lark always tries to use the first host's calendar. This can create events on the wrong calendar or fail for other hosts.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent only uses the first destination calendar for multi-host events
findings.body: Office365CalendarService.createEvent uses the first entry of event.destinationCalendar and ignores the credentialId passed by CalendarManager. For collective events with multiple destination calendars, every host's credential will attempt to create the event in the first host's calendar, which can fail or produce incorrect events for the other hosts.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent only uses the first destination calendar for multi-host events
findings.body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters calendars by the first entry of event.destinationCalendar. It does not select the destination calendar that corresponds to the credential creating the event. With multiple host destination calendars, CalDAV events for non-first hosts can be created on the wrong calendar or fail.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation only deletes the first calendar reference per booking
findings.body: When cancelling all remaining recurring bookings, the code finds only the first reference whose type includes _calendar for each updated booking and attempts deletes using the organizer's calendar credentials. Multi-host bookings can have multiple calendar references, including credentials that are not in bookingToDelete.user.credentials, so some host calendar events may not be deleted.

findings.title: Awaiting the apiDeletes array does not await deletion promises
findings.body: In the paid cancellation branch, the code executes await apiDeletes where apiDeletes is an array of promises. This does not wait for the promises or catch their rejections. Calendar or video deletions may still be running when the handler returns, and failures will not be handled by the surrounding try/catch.

findings.title: Confirming a pending collective booking only includes one destination calendar
findings.body: confirmHandler builds evt.destinationCalendar from only booking.destinationCalendar or user.destinationCalendar. It does not include destination calendars for other collective hosts. When a pending collective booking is confirmed, EventManager.create will therefore only create the organizer's calendar event, not events for all hosts.

findings.title: Webhook payload destinationCalendar is inconsistent between events
findings.body: The test expects destinationCalendar to be [] for BOOKING_REJECTED but expects null for BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED elsewhere in the same file. The migration to an array-backed destinationCalendar should use a consistent empty representation across webhook payloads to avoid breaking consumers.
